claims.text: HfNbTiVAl10 has a reported hierarchical heterostructure with multilevel chemical fluctuations.
A transformer can be pre-trained on extensive synthetic materials data and fine-tuned on alloy-specific experimental or simulation data.
Phase-diagram-inspired descriptors can encode information relevant to HEA structural stability and phase constitution.
The proposed phase-diagram descriptors encode the hierarchical chemical fluctuations of HfNbTiVAl10.
Transformer self-attention can capture intricate, nonlinear relationships among elemental interactions in HEAs.
Transformer self-attention will capture the microstructural features and multilevel chemical fluctuations that govern HfNbTiVAl10 behavior.
Combining physically motivated descriptors with a transformer embeds both structural and thermophysical information.
Transfer learning with synthetic materials data can mitigate limited experimental-data availability and improve HEA property prediction.
The proposed model will accurately predict Young's modulus for hierarchical-heterostructured HfNbTiVAl10.
The proposed model will accurately predict yield strength for hierarchical-heterostructured HfNbTiVAl10.
The proposed model will accurately predict fracture toughness for hierarchical-heterostructured HfNbTiVAl10.
The transformer will improve predictive accuracy by roughly 15–20% relative to CALPHAD and first-principles methods.
The transformer will reduce prediction runtime by at least 50% relative to CALPHAD and first-principles methods.
First-principles calculations can reliably predict at least some elastic properties of refractory HEAs.
Standard CALPHAD and first-principles approaches are computationally intensive and comparatively inefficient for predicting fracture properties.
The model may become unreliable when processing-induced microstructures differ substantially from those represented in its training data.
The model may become unreliable when its phase-diagram-inspired descriptors omit critical structural mediators.
The quantitative accuracy and runtime gains remain unvalidated, and the model may not fully capture complex fracture mechanisms.
A blinded benchmark of at least 20 independently synthesized samples, with experimental measurements and CALPHAD/first-principles controls, can test the stated performance thresholds.
